title: Reconcile Acceptance Ledger and Tear Down Proof Review Surface
description: Operator lifecycle command that materialises the acceptance ledger out of the ADR 0015 review volume into the committed evidence corpus, commits it, closes the /proof gate (restores the committed 503 default and reloads the edge), then stops only the cockpit while leaving the shared public proof edge up and preserving the ledger volume.
purpose: Persist the operator's recorded acceptance and signoff decisions from the running cockpit into the committed evidence corpus as the manual operator reconciliation step, then close the /proof cockpit gate and stop the cockpit while the shared composed public proof edge keeps serving.
outputs: A git commit reconciling the acceptance ledger from the review volume
A closed /proof gate (the committed 503 default restored on the runtime include and reloaded) with the cockpit stopped, the external-caddy edge left running, and the ledger volume preserved
sideEffects: Reads the acceptance ledger from the running cockpit Docker volume
Creates a git commit of the reconciled acceptance ledger (not pushed automatically)
Restores the committed CLOSED (503) /proof gate include on the gitignored runtime mount and reloads external-caddy to close the gate
Stops only the staging-proof-cockpit service (leaving external-caddy up so the public proof routes keep serving) and preserves the ledger volume (no volume removal)
failureSemantics: Fails closed if the cockpit service is not running or the materialised ledger is not valid JSON with at least one action; on failure nothing is committed and the surface is left for inspection. The commit records the operator's own recorded decisions and does not itself upgrade any readiness claim; final signoff remains whatever the operator recorded in the cockpit.
aiGuidance: Use this command to reconcile operator-recorded acceptance from the review volume into the committed evidence corpus, close the /proof gate, and stop the cockpit while leaving the shared composed proof edge running. It git-commits the acceptance ledger but never pushes; the running service is never given repository write credentials; it does not stop external-caddy (use caddy-down for that) and never removes the ledger volume. Do not use it to fabricate acceptance the operator did not record in the cockpit.
